refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These configuration files control NTP network time synchronization. See systemd.syntax7 for a general description of the syntax.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: The following settings are configured in the [Time] section:

listitem.para: A space-separated list of NTP server host names or IP addresses. During runtime this list is combined with any per-interface NTP servers acquired from systemd-networkd.service8. systemd-timesyncd will contact all configured system or per-interface servers in turn, until one responds. When the empty string is assigned, the list of NTP servers is reset, and all prior assignments will have no effect. This setting defaults to an empty list.

A space-separated list of NTP server host names or IP addresses to be used as the fallback NTP servers. Any per-interface NTP servers obtained from systemd-networkd.service8 take precedence over this setting, as do any servers set via NTP= above. This setting is hence only relevant if no other NTP server information is known. When the empty string is assigned, the list of NTP servers is reset, and all prior assignments will have no effect. If this option is not given, a compiled-in list of NTP servers is used.

Maximum acceptable root distance, i.e. the maximum estimated time required for a packet to travel to the server we are connected to from the server with the reference clock. If the current server does not satisfy this limit, systemd-timesyncd will switch to a different server.
Takes a time span value. The default unit is seconds, but other units may be specified, see systemd.time7. Defaults to 5 seconds.
The minimum and maximum poll intervals for NTP messages. Polling starts at the minimum poll interval, and is adjusted within the specified limits in response to received packets.

Each setting takes a time span value. The default unit is seconds, but other units may be specified, see systemd.time7. PollIntervalMinSec= defaults to 32 seconds and must not be smaller than 16 seconds. PollIntervalMaxSec= defaults to 34 min 8 s (2048 seconds) and must be larger than PollIntervalMinSec=.
Specifies the minimum delay before subsequent attempts to contact a new NTP server are made.
Takes a time span value. The default unit is seconds, but other units may be specified, see systemd.time7. Defaults to 30 seconds and must not be smaller than 1 second.

The interval at which the current time is periodically saved to disk, in the absence of any recent synchronisation from an NTP server. This is especially useful for offline systems with no local RTC, as it will guarantee that the system clock remains roughly monotonic across reboots.
Takes a time interval value. The default unit is seconds, but other units may be specified, see systemd.time7. Defaults to 60 seconds.

Takes a boolean or the absolute path of a device node below /dev/. Many hypervisors and cloud providers expose their notion of the current time to virtual machines as a PTP hardware clock (PHC) device, for example /dev/ptp_kvm (KVM, requires the ptp_kvm kernel module), /dev/ptp_hyperv (Hyper-V and Azure), /dev/ptp_vmware (VMware), and /dev/ptp_ena (Amazon EC2). If enabled and such a device is available, the system clock is synchronized to it instead of to an NTP server: it is read every 2 seconds and NTP servers are not contacted while it is in use. Defaults to true. If the empty string is assigned, the default is restored.

Only PTP hardware clock devices that carry the udev tag timesync are considered. The default udev rules set this tag on the hypervisor devices listed above. Additional devices may be tagged with a udev rule such as SUBSYSTEM=="ptp", ATTR{clock_name}=="…", TAG+="timesync" and the tag may be removed from a device with TAG-="timesync" to exclude it. Note that despite the name the Precision Time Protocol is not implemented: tagged devices must be local clocks that report UTC (as is the case for the hypervisor devices listed above), not network interface clocks synchronized via PTP, which typically run on TAI.

If a device node path is specified (for example /dev/ptp_kvm or /dev/ptp0), the PTP hardware clock whose device node or one of whose device node symlinks matches the path is used instead, regardless of whether it carries the timesync tag. Only that device is considered then.

The first suitable device that may be read successfully is used, including devices that show up later at runtime, as long as no device is in use yet. If the device goes away, is not suitable anymore (i.e. loses the tag, or the configured device node path), or cannot be read anymore, the next suitable device is tried, and if there is none, NTP is used.
